name: Step Finance
rootCause: Step Finance, a Solana analytics and DeFi dashboard platform, lost approximately $27.3 million (261,854 SOL) on January 31, 2026 when attackers compromised the private keys of executive team members through a targeted social engineering and device-compromise campaign. The attackers — reportedly linked to the Lazarus Group — conducted reconnaissance on Step Finance executives through professional networks and social media, then delivered tailored phishing campaigns disguised as legitimate business communications. Once an executive's device was compromised, the attackers extracted authentication tokens and signing credentials, gaining control over Step Finance's treasury and fee wallets. They then unstaked 261,854 SOL from Solana staking accounts (a process that was not protected by smart-contract-level multi-sig) and transferred the funds to unknown addresses. Token22/Remora tools later allowed recovery of approximately $4.7M, but the bulk (~$27M) was irrecoverable. The incident was not a smart-contract bug — the vulnerable surface was the operational security of key custodians and their devices. Attack Date: January 31, 2026 Root Cause: Compromised executive device via targeted phishing/social engineering; private keys for treasury wallets exfiltrated off-chain. Attack Tx (CertiK on-chain evidence): SOL unstaking and transfer of 261,854 SOL from Step Finance treasury wallets to unknown addresses. Analysis: CoinDesk Halborn MEXC News

descriptions.text: Audited contracts, bug bounties, and security reviews. None of it mattered when an executive's inbox at Step Finance became the attack vector. $27.3 million in SOL unstaked and gone. The smart contracts worked flawlessly. The humans didn't.

Step Finance has issued a statement on X regarding a recent exploit, disclosing that approximately $40 million was stolen from its treasury due to a compromise of an executive's device. Upon detecting the vulnerability, Step Finance launched an investigation in collaboration with cybersecurity researchers and relevant authorities, and has notified law enforcement. While certain operations were temporarily suspended during this period, the team has successfully recovered approximately $3.7 million in Remora assets and $1 million in other positions.

Step Finance suffered a catastrophic treasury drain on Solana on 31 January 2026 after attacker(s) compromised executive devices and gained control of protocol-critical private keys. An estimated $40 million was drained from treasury and fee wallets, primarily via unstaked SOL. The platform and its affiliated products shut down, with partial asset recovery but no smart contract involvement. The endpoint devices of Step Finance's executive team were compromised, likely via targeted phishing or social engineering. This breach allowed attackers to seize private keys and rotate stake authority, leading to full control over treasury assets and operational wallets.…

The Solana-based defi portfolio tracker Step Finance lost 261,854 SOL (~$28.7 million) when a thief gained access to treasury and fee wallets. It's not yet clear how the attacker was able to steal the funds, although Step Finance posted to Twitter that the theft occurred via a "well known attack vector". Step wrote that they were working with cybersecurity firms and law enforcement to address the incident.
